Subject: Physical transfer runbook for islanded clusters

Hi Jamie / Acme ops team —

Attaching a draft runbook for the physical media transfer workflow we discussed for islanded (air‑isolated) customer clusters. High level: physical handoff -> manifest reconciliation -> cryptographic attestation -> sealed-storage ingress — all designed to avoid any online sync.

What I need from you: please review the runbook and the manifest template and call out gaps around courier chain-of-custody, tamper-evident sealing, and any on-site handoff constraints that could affect our staging/validate windows.

Key constraints we have from product/security:
- Two-person control for signing manifests (dual approval)
- HSM-wrapped signing keys: hardware-backed master key stored in customer HSM, with Redwood signing key wrapped at origin
- Zero-touch verification on the islanded node: SHA256 sums, PGP/cosign-style signature checked locally before install
- Burn-in window: 2 hour staging node validation before cutover

Attachments: runbook_v0.9.pdf (full draft), transfer_manifest_template.csv

Proposed timeline: dry run week of Oct 12, production window Oct 19–20.

Thanks — please reply with any blocking concerns.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Strategic Ops (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Physical transfer runbook for islanded clusters

Thanks Vanessa — quick read and a couple of notes: we like the flow and the manifest fields. A few clarifications before we sign off internally: 

1) Courier sealing: our current courier partners support serialized tamper seals (S-serial) and a chain-of-custody PDF. Do you require an independent notary step at handoff? That adds time but is doable for high‑sensitivity installs.

2) Signatures: you mentioned PGP/cosign. We can produce cosign signatures (sigstore) from an ephemeral keypair generated at origin, but for enterprise customers that require hardware-backed provenance we recommend an HSM-signed attestation. Is Redwood able to accept a cosign attestation wrapped by an HSM signature (attestation-of-attestation)?

3) Manifest reconciliation: suggest adding a quick checksum column per file (SHA256) and a scanned receipt photo field to reduce disputes at handoff.

I've attached a short courier-seal-spec.pdf that lists the tamper-seal options we can provide.

If you want, we can do a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk through the dry-run checklist.

—Jamie
Edge Integrations — Solutions
Attachment: courier-seal-spec.pdf

Thanks for the draft — good coverage. A few internal requirements to bake into the runbook before we send back to the customer: 

- Dual‑signer rule: both Redwood Ops lead and customer on‑site security must sign the manifest. That needs a covered workflow for when the on‑site signer is remote (delegation with signed authorization PDF).
- HSM/KMS flow: we require the wrapped signing key to be generated in Redwood's build environment, wrapped by the customer's HSM public key, and included with the media in a sealed HSM‑wrapped envelope. Add a key rotation note: rotate the wrapping key quarterly or after any physical incident. I've added hsm-key-rotation-notes.txt to the attachments.
- Acceptance tests: include a pre-install verification run (hashes + signature validation) and a post-install smoke test. Failure modes must specify safe rollback to staging image preserved on local air‑storage.

Also: propose a dry run that exercises the full manifest flow end-to-end with our courier partner and Edge Integrations. If we can get a signed liability waiver from the customer, we can run a single trial without a notary.

Marissa
Head of Private Deployments (temp)
Redwood Inference

Looping in a couple of technical clarifications from infra: 

- Image signing format: we support cosign signatures (SHA256) and PGP; for HSM workflows we will accept a PKCS#7 envelope or an HSM-wrapped cosign key. On the target node we'll run a local verifier that accepts a hierarchy: customer HSM root -> wrapped Redwood signing key -> image signature.
- Manifest schema: I've filled the template with an example and included transfer_manifest_filled.csv. Please confirm we want the following fields: filename, size_bytes, sha256, signature_type, signer_id, seal_serial, on_site_contact_name, on_site_contact_phone, photo_receipt_url.
- Burn-in/validate: infra requires 120 minutes of isolated burn-in, with logs exported to a USB blob (encrypt with customer public key) and hash recorded on the manifest.

We also need the on-site contact's public SSH key and a local admin contact for the staging node. If the customer cannot provide that, we will coordinate with Edge Integrations for an accredited on-site technician (their additional SOW).

Attachment: transfer_manifest_filled.csv

1) Acceptable attestation path: we will accept cosign signatures wrapped with HSM testimony (attestation-of-attestation). Dev will publish the verifier spec (expected input: PKCS#7 or cosign+wrapped-key) by EOD Friday.

2) Dry run: agreed on Oct 14, 09:00–13:00 PT. Objective: end-to-end manifest signing, courier handoff, local verification, 2 hour burn-in. Edge Integrations to provide courier with tamper seals; AcmeCloud to confirm on-site contact.

3) Deliverables before dry run (owners):
- Final runbook (Vanessa): update dual-signer flow and notary optional path.
- Verifier spec (Dev): publish on Drive and add to runbook.
- Courier SLA + seals (Jamie): confirm serial format and provide sample seal IDs.
- Manifest prefill and sample on-site contact (Marcus): coordinate with customer ops.

4) Compliance note (Marissa): include key rotation table and incident escalation matrix in runbook (we will add appendix B).

I've attached the current artifacts for the thread. If there are no blockers I'll circulate the final runbook after the dry run and push a signed copy to the customer's DocuSign envelope (DocuSign:0xA1B2-Courier-Agreement).
